chapters.name: Management of Care
chapters.summary: Prioritizing care, delegation and assignment, advocacy, client rights, informed consent, confidentiality, legal and ethical duties, continuity of care, and working with the care team.
keyPoints: Prioritize airway, breathing, circulation and unstable clients first
Delegate only stable, routine tasks with predictable outcomes
Informed consent is the provider's duty; the nurse witnesses it

chapters.name: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
chapters.summary: Standard and transmission-based precautions, client identification, fall and restraint safety, medical and surgical asepsis, reporting incidents, ergonomics, and emergency response.

chapters.name: Growth, Development and Childbearing Care
chapters.summary: Normal growth and development across the lifespan, antepartum, intrapartum and postpartum care, and newborn care.
keyPoints: Normal pregnancy changes and danger signs

chapters.name: Health Screening and Disease Prevention
chapters.summary: Health screening, immunizations, health risk factors, health teaching, and self-care.

chapters.name: Therapeutic Communication, Coping and Crisis
chapters.summary: Therapeutic communication, coping with illness and loss, grief, crisis intervention, abuse and neglect, and cultural awareness.

chapters.name: Mental Health Conditions and Substance Use
chapters.summary: Care of clients with anxiety, mood, psychotic and cognitive disorders, suicide risk, substance use and withdrawal, and a safe therapeutic environment.

chapters.name: Basic Care and Comfort
chapters.summary: Mobility and immobility, elimination, nutrition and oral hydration, personal hygiene, rest and sleep, and non-drug comfort measures.

chapters.name: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies
chapters.summary: Medication administration and calculation, adverse effects and interactions, high-alert medications, blood products, IV therapy and central lines, and pain management.

chapters.name: Reduction of Risk Potential
chapters.summary: Changes in vital signs, laboratory values, diagnostic tests and their preparation, potential complications of procedures and surgery, and system-specific assessments.

chapters.name: Physiological Adaptation
chapters.summary: Care of clients with acute, chronic or life-threatening conditions: fluid and electrolyte imbalances, hemodynamics, respiratory and cardiac emergencies, and medical emergencies.
